source.text: Λέγω αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔτι μοι τοῦτο δήλωσον. Τί, φησίν, ἐπιζητεῖς; Εἰ ἄρα, φημί, κύριε, τὸν αὐτὸν χρόνον βασανίζονται οἱ τρυφῶντες καὶ ἀπατώμενοι, ὅσον τ ἀπάτης ὁ χρόνος ὥρα ἐστὶ μία· τῆς δὲ βασάνου ἡ ὥρα τριάκοντα ἡμερῶν δύναμιν ἔχει. ἐὰν οὖν μίαν ἡμέραν τρυφήσῃ τις καὶ ἀπατηθῇ, μίαν δὲ ἡμέραν βασανισθῇ, ὅλον ἐνιαυτὸν ἰσχύει ἡ ἡμέρα τῆς βασάνου. ὅσας οὖν ἡμέρας τρυφήσῃ τις, τοσούτους ἐνιαυτοὺς βασανίζεται. βλέπεις οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι τῆς τρυφῆς καὶ ἀπάτης ὁ χρόνος ἐλάχιστός ἐστι, τῆς δὲ τιμωρίας καὶ βασάνου πολύς.

translation.text: I say to him, "Lord, explain this to me further." He says, "What are you seeking?" I say, "Are then, Lord, those who indulge and are deceived tormented for the same amount of time as the time of the deceit? It is one hour, but the hour of the torment has the force of thirty days. Therefore, if someone indulges for one day and is deceived, and is tormented for one day, the day of torment is equivalent to a whole year. So then, as many days as a person indulges, for that many years he is tormented." "You see then," he says, "that the time of indulgence and deception is very small, but the time of punishment and torment is great."

base_translation.text: I say to him, "Lord, explain this to me further." He says, "What are you seeking?" I say, "Then, Lord, are those who indulge themselves and are deceived tormented for the same length of time as the time of the deception? For the time of deception is one hour, but the hour of torment has the force of thirty days. Therefore, if someone indulges himself for one day and is deceived, and is tormented for one day, the day of torment amounts to a whole year. So then, for as many days as a person indulges himself, for that many years he is tormented." "You see then," he says, "that the time of indulgence and deception is very short, but the time of punishment and torment is long."

translation.text:
I said to him, “Lord, explain this more fully to me.”

He asked, “What do you want to know?”

I said, “Then, Lord, are those who give themselves over to pleasure and are deceived tormented for the same amount of time as their deception? The time of deception is one hour, but one hour of torment counts as thirty days. So if someone gives himself over to pleasure for one day, is deceived, and is tormented for one day, that one day of torment counts as a whole year. Therefore, for every day a person gives himself over to pleasure, that person is tormented for a year.”

He said, “You see, then, that the time of pleasure and deception is very short, but the time of punishment and torment is long.”

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: What do you want to know?
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: He asks what further explanation the speaker wants.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The plain question naturally expresses a request for understanding.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: those who give themselves over to pleasure
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: They yield themselves to self-indulgent pleasure rather than merely enjoying ordinary pleasure.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB controlling translation and grounding review
simplification_decisions.rationale: This wording preserves the negative, deliberate force without suggesting that all enjoyment is wrong.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: the day of torment amounts to a whole year
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: that one day of torment counts as a whole year
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The passage equates one day of torment with a full year in its calculation.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Counts as” makes the unusual proportion easier to follow.

risk_flags.risk: The relationship between indulgence, deception, and the time calculation may remain difficult.
risk_flags.mitigation: The hour-to-thirty-days example and the day-to-year conclusion are both stated explicitly.

I said to him, “Lord, explain this more fully to me.”

He asked, “What do you want to know?”

I said, “Lord, then are those who live for pleasure and are deceived tormented according to how long their deception lasted? One hour of deception results in thirty days of torment. So if someone lives for pleasure and is deceived for one day, then is tormented for one day, that day of torment counts as a whole year. Therefore, for every day a person lives for pleasure, that person is tormented for a year.”

He said, “You see, then, that the time of pleasure and deception is very short, but the time of punishment and torment is long.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and preserves the passage’s warning and its disproportionate time calculation. Revision is needed because it adds “for one day” to the deception itself, whereas the example and conclusion expressly calculate according to days of indulgence. The replacement retains the useful plain-language dialogue and “counts as” explanation while preserving that distinction.
